body.statement: There are constants \(C_1,C_2<\infty\), depending only on \(s,M,v,\alpha\), such that if \(T_n\ge C_1\log(e/\kappa_n)\), then \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}\) is uniformly honest over \(\mathcal P_n\) and \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P[|I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}|]\le C_2\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}.\] Consequently \(L_n(\kappa_n)\asymp L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)\) in this region, uniformly over vanishing \(\kappa_n\). This strictly extends the fixed-jump oracle conclusion of Porter and Yu (2015) by allowing \(\kappa_n\to0\) down to the stated boundary and by delivering uniform honest connected-interval length.
body.justification: This theorem supplies an implementable honest procedure using only observable one-sided regressions and pins the region in which cutoff estimation is asymptotically costless for interval length.
body.gap: PorterYu2015 obtains oracle effect estimation after an unknown fixed jump, while NoackRothe2024 obtains weak-first-stage honesty at a known cutoff; neither result covers an unknown cutoff with \(\kappa_n\to0\).
body.consumer: Applied researchers obtain a data procedure that recovers the known-cutoff honest length once treatment uptake contains enough localization information.
